title: Cast Iron Chicken Fajitas
seoTitle: Cast Iron Chicken Fajitas | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Sizzling peppers and chicken with warm tortillas for ten
subtitle: Sizzling peppers and chicken with warm tortillas for ten
description: Chicken strips marinate in lime and spices, sear hot in cast iron with peppers and onions, and serve sizzling with warm tortillas and classic fixings. Built for build-your-own line speed.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Cast Iron Chicken Fajitas in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.instruction: Toss chicken strips with lime juice, 2 tablespoons olive oil, chili powder, cumin, and garlic. Marinate at least 30 minutes in the fridge.

steps.title: Sear the chicken
steps.instruction: Heat cast iron over high heat until smoking lightly. Sear chicken in batches 3–4 minutes until charred edges appear and internal temp reaches 165°F. Set aside.

steps.title: Char the vegetables
steps.instruction: Add remaining oil to the pan. Sear peppers and onions 4–5 minutes until blistered and tender-crisp with light char. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Combine and season
steps.instruction: Return chicken to pan, toss with vegetables, and season with salt to balance. Squeeze half a lime over the mix. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Cast Iron Chicken Fajitas onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 10 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Serve sizzling
steps.instruction: Warm tortillas wrapped in foil at 300°F for 10 minutes. Portion chicken and peppers into hot cast iron skillets or hotel pans and serve with fixings. Target oven/smoker temperature: 300°F. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

proTips: Vent the kitchen—high-heat searing sets off alarms if you are not ready.
A splash of chicken broth at the end keeps everything juicy on the hold line.
Offer sliced jalapeños for heat without forcing spice on the whole hall.
tonightSpread: Sizzling fajita pans with tortillas, shredded cheese, salsa, and sour cream.
Spanish rice on the side for crew who want a plated option instead of wraps.
leftovers: Chop into breakfast burritos with scrambled eggs and hot sauce.
Toss cold leftovers over romaine for a quick fajita salad lunch.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Fajitas feel like an event—sizzling pans, fresh toppings, everyone building their own. Interactive meals keep morale up on long tour days.
mealPrepNotes: Slice chicken uniform for even cooking. Marinate up to 8 hours. Warm tortillas in foil bundles so they stay soft at the line.
